meta.name: Track SERP layout changes with Snapshot Site, Google Sheets, and Slack

name: Track Search Results Page (SERP) Layout Changes with Screenshots → Slack

parameters.content:
## Track Search Results Page (SERP) Layout Changes with Screenshots → Slack

### How it works

Every morning this workflow reads a keyword list from a Google Sheet (`url`, `keyword`, `country`, `language`, `baselineUrl`) and loops over it one keyword at a time. For each row it captures the **above-the-fold** slice of that search-results URL with Snapshot Site **Screenshot** — `country` and `language` come straight from the sheet row, because a SERP is geo- and language-specific — then runs a **Compare** of that fresh capture against the row's stored baseline SERP image. Each keyword produces one compact result row (keyword, country, raw mismatch percentage, diff link, `stable`/`shifted`/`failed`); a keyword that errors is recorded as `failed` and the loop keeps going. On the loop's Done branch a Code node sorts by mismatch percentage and posts **one** Slack digest listing the keywords whose SERP layout actually moved — new ad blocks, an AI answer box, a featured snippet, or a local pack pushing the organic results down.

### Setup steps

- Install the `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site` community node (Settings → Community nodes → Install → `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site`) — verified by n8n.
- Add a Snapshot Site credential, a Google Sheets credential, and a Slack credential.
- **Check the terms of service of whatever search engine you point this at.** Automated capture of search results pages can conflict with those terms, and engines actively bot-gate automated requests, so captures may come back as consent walls or CAPTCHAs. Where an official SERP API exists, prefer it for ranking data — this workflow is for the visual layout a human sees.
- Create a **Keywords** tab and type this header row in literally, one column per cell: `url`, `keyword`, `country`, `language`, `baselineUrl`. Cell **A1 must contain the literal text `url`**, not a URL — otherwise Sheets treats the URL as the column name and every capture fails with `URL is required`.
- Fill one row per keyword: `url` = the **full** search-results URL including `https://` (the API rejects bare domains), `keyword` = the human label used in the digest, `country`/`language` = the region and language to render the SERP for (e.g. `us` / `en`), `baselineUrl` = the URL of a hosted baseline screenshot of that SERP.
- Capture each baseline with the **same** `width`, `height`, `country`, and `language` as `Capture SERP Above the Fold` uses, or the comparison mostly measures dimension differences instead of layout changes.
- Point **Read Keyword List** at your spreadsheet, set the channels on both Slack nodes, and adjust the schedule.

### Customization

Raise or lower the shift threshold (`10`%) in **Record SERP Result** — SERP layout changes are gross, so `10` is the sensible band and `> 0` would fire on every rotating ad. Change `height` (1200 today) to match the fold you care about, add rows for more keywords or more countries per keyword, or replace the Slack digest with Google Sheets/Airtable rows to build a history of SERP layout volatility per keyword.

## Schedule and read the keyword list

Runs once a day and reads every tracked keyword from the Google Sheet — one row per search-results URL, with its own country and language.
The loop processes one keyword per iteration so a bot-gated or slow SERP never blocks the rest of the sweep.

## Capture the SERP, compare it, and handle errors

One Screenshot call per keyword (`country`/`language` from the sheet row, `fullSize: false` with an explicit `height` so only the competitive above-the-fold real estate is captured), then one Compare against the stored baseline SERP image.
Hard failures (error output) and soft failures (`{error: true}` on the success output — including a consent wall that returns an API error) both become a `failed` row and go back into the loop. A single failing keyword must never abort the sweep.

## Report one SERP digest result

After the loop's Done branch, keywords are sorted by mismatch percentage descending and rendered as a single Slack message with raw percentages and diff image links.
A quiet day sends a short all-clear line, so silence means "workflow broken", not "nothing moved".
